source_notes.label: Compare two acid-specific hydrothermal preparations
source_notes.summary: The study deliberately changes acid identity, initial pH and hydrothermal temperature to obtain two anatase colloids with similar primary sizes. Sample 1 uses acetic acid at pH 2 and 280 °C; sample 2 uses nitric acid at pH 1.9 and 250 °C. The authors interpret later solution-behavior differences in terms of surface structure; the prior facet study is cited, not independently remeasured here.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 1–2, 6, Introduction, Colloid Synthesis and surface discussion

source_notes.label: Each size method describes a different object or estimator
source_notes.summary: TEM reports number-average projected particle dimensions; XRD reports volume-average coherent crystallite sizes. DLS measures solvated, aggregated hydrodynamic dimensions. AUC sizes calculated using bulk anatase density and later hydration-model core sizes are derived interpretations, not interchangeable direct particle measurements.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 2–5, Figures 1–5 and DLS/model discussion

source_notes.label: Analytical pH reveals different aggregation responses
source_notes.summary: Both samples are already aggregated at pH 1 according to the authors. Sample 2 shows strong aggregation between pH 1.96 and 1.99, whereas sample 1 follows a different sedimentation trend despite similar zeta potentials below the point of zero charge. These pH settings characterize the prepared colloids; they do not create extra synthesis recipe–structure pairs.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 3–5, Figures 3–5 and DLS block

source_notes.label: Hydration shells are a qualified model
source_notes.summary: The authors combine DLS and AUC under hard-sphere and negligible-charge assumptions to infer an apparent hydrated density. Their spherical anatase-core/water-shell illustration is explicitly inadequate for aggregates, and shape cannot be separated from hydration using AUC alone. The last model row is printed as sample 1 at pH 1.96 although related DLS/density and conclusion statements concern sample 2; the assignment remains unresolved.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 5–6, Equation 4, model list and limitations

source_notes.label: A future combined method is not a performed experiment
source_notes.summary: Flow field-flow fractionation coupled to AUC is proposed as future work to disentangle size, shape, hydration and charge distributions. It is not an additional demonstrated preparation or measurement series in this contribution.
